teaser.text: Next plc is a British retailer selling clothes, footwear and home products through shops and digital channels. It also earns money by helping other brands sell, deliver and finance their goods.

stock.title: NEXT stock forecast
stock.meta_description: NEXT stock forecast: the weighted outcome is modest over one year and positive by the third year, driven by growth, execution and cash conversion.
stock.opening: At October 2029, NEXT's weighted price reaches 16512.87 GBp, a 14% gain including dividends. The forecast hinges on warehouse execution and cash conversion.
stock.closing: The full memo also answers what NEXT does, who its rivals are, how management is executing and what risks could change the outcome.

blocks.heading: Where could NEXT's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: NEXT's weighted outcome is modest over one year, but becomes positive by the third year. At October 2027, the weighted price is 14379.15 GBp, a 5% loss including dividends. At October 2028, it is 15324.14 GBp, a 4% gain. At October 2029, it reaches 16512.87 GBp, a 14% gain.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for NEXT, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: The bear case requires weak UK demand, lower overseas conversion and rising marketing, returns and delivery costs. Warehouse investment arrives before sufficient volume, cash conversion weakens and buybacks slow. The price falls to 11431.07 GBp in October 2027 and 10078.22 GBp in October 2029. Its 25% probability reflects credible margin pressure and downside from today's elevated valuation.

The bull case requires international growth without margin dilution. Repeat customers reduce acquisition costs, warehouse automation improves fulfilment economics and Total Platform develops repeatable service profit. The price reaches 17308.37 GBp in 2027 and 25592.37 GBp in 2029. Its 20% probability reflects the need for several execution gains while marketing and capital spending rise.

blocks.heading: How much cash does NEXT really make?

paragraphs.text: Operating cash was £1,233.6 million in January 2026. After capital spending, lease payments and interest, free cash flow was £800.9 million. Rent must be included because a retailer still pays landlords even when accounting rules place much of the lease cost outside operating cash flow.

Employee share awards also have an economic cost. Deducting £43.1 million of stock pay produces real free cash flow of £757.8 million. This is an analytical measure, not a statutory subtotal, and the same cost must not be deducted twice.

blocks.heading: How much does NEXT pay per share?

paragraphs.text: Dividends rise from the latest £2.68 per share to £3.00 in the base case, then £3.30 and £3.60. The path is slower than the latest 15% increase because the low-base effect fades, but it is supported by the £319m ordinary-dividend plan and £752m of forecast surplus cash before distributions.

blocks.heading: What is NEXT's dividend yield at today's price?

paragraphs.text: At 15,380.00p on 16 October 2026, one share costs £153.80. The market values the equity at £18,403.2m, while the trailing price-to-earnings ratio, or P/E, is 19.56x. A P/E says how many pounds investors pay for each pound of annual earnings. The forward P/E is 17.46x because expected earnings are higher, so growth is already part of the purchase price.

The forward P/E of 17.46x implies an earnings yield of roughly 5.7%. That is profit attributed to the share, not cash paid to its owner. An illustrative 10% annual return could combine about 8% annual earnings-per-share growth with the 1.7% dividend yield, if the valuation multiple stayed unchanged.
